blocks.heading: Choosing promotion for the case
blocks.text: A promotion choice depends on objective, target access, product complexity, budget, stage of awareness and the obstacle to purchase. An unfamiliar taste may suit sampling; a complex high-value machine may need personal explanation; a local simple offer may need an accessible concise advert. Compare the strongest alternative and include cost and capacity. A campaign that creates orders beyond supply can disappoint customers. Do not choose television merely because it is widely known or claim that a modern medium is universally effective.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Fictional Omi Tea has a small local budget and buyers are uncertain about a new flavour. It can offer controlled samples at its existing collection point. Sampling directly addresses taste uncertainty and reaches relevant buyers. A broad expensive campaign may create awareness without resolving that barrier. Prefer a limited sample trial with clear buying information and review paid sales; protect hygiene, cost and capacity.
